tasks.short: Model marketing costs, conversions and revenue to forecast outcomes and compare spending choices.

steps.what: Export campaign costs, conversions and recognised revenue.
Align periods, currencies, campaign identifiers and revenue definitions in the forecast workbook.
Agree conversion, margin, seasonality and spending assumptions with finance and marketing.
Build revenue scenarios and sensitivity calculations in the forecast workbook.
Challenge model logic, reconcile totals and accept the financial assumptions.
Review scenarios and approve a planning forecast.

tasks.design: Adapters load permitted extracts from the {ADS}, {CRM}, {ECOMMERCE} and {ERP} into a versioned forecast dataset on the {DATA_PLATFORM}. A deterministic scenario generator produces a checked {SPREADSHEET} workbook and a {BI} view, with explicit assumptions, reconciliation exceptions and forecast limitations. Finance validates the model and the marketing manager approves its use in planning.
tasks.previous_blocker: Campaign identifiers, revenue definitions and attribution windows differ across systems. Bespoke workbook maintenance often costs less initially than building reliable adapters.
tasks.enabler_now: Reusable adapters, formula libraries and automated reconciliation checks are easier to build and maintain with coding assistance. No model breakthrough is required.
tasks.still_hard: Attribution does not establish incremental revenue. Sparse history, changing auctions and uncertain margins still require judgement; GDPR constrains customer-level joins.
tasks.human_edge: Choose credible commercial assumptions, recognise structural changes and challenge attractive forecasts with weak causal support.

ambition.what: Weekly marginal-spend scenario review during active campaigns

tasks.altitude: Less time goes into workbook assembly; more goes into testing assumptions and explaining uncertainty. The strategist can initiate weekly scenario reviews, while finance validation and budget authority remain with their existing owners.

reach.learn: Contribution margin, incremental return and the company's spending approval limits

evidence.claim: Structured inputs, explicit assumptions and fixed formulas support deterministic scenario generation.
Commercial assumptions and causal interpretation still need human judgement; the digest provides no direct marketing-forecasting case.

assumptions: Scope is one reusable forecast model with scheduled refreshes, rather than a company-wide planning replacement.
Step shares, remaining time and build ranges are planning estimates, not measured results.
The structured-input prior is credible; the under-half rule-coverage prior mainly concerns assumptions rather than arithmetic.
Aggregate data is sufficient for the first version; no employee monitoring is introduced.
unknowns: Which source systems and export permissions are available?
Are margins, refunds, revenue recognition and campaign identifiers consistently recorded?
Who accepts financial assumptions and who approves planning forecasts?
Do existing contracts and GDPR arrangements permit the proposed data joins?
research_questions: How accurately does the current forecast predict revenue across campaign cycles?
Which existing forecasting and export features can remove custom development?
Which assumptions explain most forecast error?
new_work: Resolve unmatched campaign identifiers and reconciliation exceptions.
Compare forecasts with realised outcomes and revise assumptions.
Maintain adapters, measurement definitions and calculation tests.
Review access and retention when adding customer-level data.

tasks.short: Implement consistent online enquiry handling, service guidance and escalation processes.

steps.what: Review online enquiries, complaints and service metrics to identify recurring failures.

loop.input: A permitted, minimised ticket sample and an approved service issue taxonomy
loop.output: Issue labels and a summary linked to ticket references
loop.check: Validate labels against the taxonomy; review a sample and all uncertain or severe cases.
loop.stop: One classification pass and one correction pass per batch; unresolved cases enter the review queue.
loop.why_not_simpler: Free-text descriptions express the same service failure in different ways; existing ticket fields may be incomplete.

steps.what: Agree response promises, handoffs and escalation ownership with the service team.
Draft service procedures, response templates and escalation guidance.

loop.input: Service process decisions, approved service facts and controlled document templates
loop.output: Procedure and response drafts with source references and explicit gaps
loop.check: Check promises, escalation ownership and factual claims against approved inputs.
loop.stop: One draft and one revision per document; missing policy decisions return to the service manager.
loop.why_not_simpler: Customer-facing wording and explanations vary by issue; fixed fields alone do not produce clear guidance.

steps.what: Configure intake forms, routing, service timers and response templates in a test environment.
Trial customer journeys and check routing, accessibility and escalation behaviour.
Approve and publish the service process after resolving blocking defects.

tasks.design: Use existing forms, queues, timers and templates in the {HELPDESK}, connected to the {CMS}. Small bounded loops summarise permitted ticket samples and draft guidance from approved policy; configured workflows handle acknowledgements and routing. The service manager approves publication, and the {BI} tracks missed promises and repeat contacts.
tasks.previous_blocker: Service promises and ownership were often unclear, while recurring problems were buried in ticket text. Teams maintained guidance separately from live queue settings.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing service configuration handles most execution. Bounded text classification and drafting reduce the cost of preparing changes and keeping guidance consistent.
tasks.still_hard: Staff capacity, unhappy customers and contested ownership remain human problems. GDPR limits ticket reuse; national rules may require employee consultation if individual service monitoring changes.
tasks.human_edge: Set realistic service promises, hear frustration and negotiate handoffs that teams can actually sustain.

ambition.what: After-hours enquiry intake with accurate acknowledgements and next-shift routing

tasks.altitude: The strategist spends more time diagnosing broken customer journeys and running service trials. They can propose and test process changes; customer service management retains authority over promises and release.

reach.task: Improve enquiry forms and service status messages
reach.learn: Accessible forms, error recovery and usability testing

reach.task: Align campaign promises with service capacity
reach.learn: Queue capacity, service commitments and campaign demand planning

evidence.claim: Configured queues, timers, acknowledgements and templates can implement repeatable service processes.
Free-text issue classification and policy-grounded drafting suit bounded loops; the digest supplies no direct case for this service redesign.

assumptions: Scope covers one online enquiry journey using an existing service system.
Step shares, remaining time and build ranges are planning estimates.
This task implements service processes; it does not replace all customer conversations.
Existing service features are checked before adding code.
The access range includes consultation where national rules require it; a formal process may take longer.
The future loops assist internal preparation rather than autonomously resolve complaints.
unknowns: Which routing, testing and publication features are already available?
Who can approve customer promises and queue changes?
Can ticket samples be used for analysis under existing GDPR arrangements?
Would the change introduce individual employee monitoring or require consultation under national rules?
What service capacity exists outside normal working hours?
research_questions: Which enquiry journeys cause the most repeat contact or abandonment?
Do current ticket categories already provide enough detail without a model loop?
Can representatives complete the proposed process under realistic queue pressure?
Does acknowledgement wording accurately describe when a person will respond?
new_work: Review uncertain ticket labels and severe issues.
Approve wording and maintain source policies.
Resolve routing exceptions and monitor missed service promises.
Retest forms and templates after policy or queue changes.
Maintain ticket minimisation, access and retention controls.

tasks.short: Develop and release transactional web features with validated forms, system connections and reliable transaction handling.

steps.what: Clarify the transaction journey and acceptance criteria with the business owner.
Configure reusable transaction components and identify gaps requiring code.
Write custom interface and transaction logic in the development environment.

loop.input: Approved implementation brief, permitted code context and established component patterns
loop.output: A reviewable code patch and relevant test changes
loop.check: Run compilation, static checks and behaviour tests; developer reviews transaction and security logic.
loop.stop: At most three patch-and-check cycles per bounded change; unresolved failures return to the developer.
loop.why_not_simpler: Native configuration and templates cover standard components, but remaining bespoke behaviour requires code synthesis.

steps.what: Connect transaction records to downstream systems using the integration development environment.
Test transactions, permissions, retries and failure recovery using the software test environment.
Accept the customer journey after checking usability, content and transaction outcomes.
Approve and deploy the accepted version through the software release environment.

tasks.design: Configure native transaction components in the {ECOMMERCE} and {CMS}, then generate only the missing code in an {OTHER} development environment through bounded patch-and-test loops. Deterministic adapters connect approved fields to the {CRM} and {ERP}; configured checks test permissions, duplicate submissions and recovery. Business acceptance and technical release approval gate deployment.
tasks.previous_blocker: Small transaction features still required developer time, integration knowledge and a complete release path. Bespoke code accumulated where native components were overlooked.
tasks.enabler_now: Coding assistance can draft bounded patches, while reusable components and established test runners handle much of the implementation and verification.
tasks.still_hard: Authorisation, transaction integrity, accessibility and unusual failure paths remain expensive to verify. GDPR applies to personal data, and generated code can pass superficial tests while retaining serious defects.
tasks.human_edge: Define a useful transaction journey, recognise unsafe shortcuts and judge whether customers can recover from failures.

ambition.what: Self-service repeat-order request for existing business customers

tasks.altitude: The strategist spends more time specifying and validating customer journeys, with developers focused on difficult behaviour and integration defects. The strategist can accept business outcomes; technical deployment and security authority remain with the technical lead.

reach.learn: Interaction states, keyboard access, validation and error recovery

reach.task: Validate order capture and fulfilment handoffs
reach.learn: Order states, pricing sources and duplicate-transaction prevention

evidence.claim: Native transaction components and deterministic integrations can reduce bespoke application work.
Bounded coding loops can draft patches checked by tests and developer review; the digest provides no direct application-development case.

assumptions: Scope is one small transaction flow on an existing website, with established identity and release facilities.
Native order and payment facilities are reused; building a payment-processing platform is outside the estimate.
Step shares, remaining time and build ranges are planning estimates.
The model loop is used during development; the live transaction path is deterministic.
In a mid-size company, a developer usually implements code while the strategist supplies requirements and acceptance.
The creation-heavy prior is credible, but development and testing typically use system screens rather than ordinary documents.
Any applicable employee consultation under national rules concerns changed work or monitoring; none is assumed automatically.
unknowns: Which native transaction components and interface contracts exist?
Are development, test and production environments separated?
Who can accept the business journey and approve deployment?
Are authentication, payment, tax and fulfilment services already available?
What code access, data-processing terms and security review requirements apply?
research_questions: Can existing configuration eliminate the custom feature?
Which failure cases could create duplicate orders, lost requests or unauthorised access?
Can the proposed coding loop pass representative transaction and permission tests?
What rollback and post-release checks are needed for this specific flow?
new_work: Review generated patches and dependency changes.
Maintain interface contracts and meaningful transaction tests.
Recheck accessibility and data access after changes.

tasks.short: Define usable, commercially sound and secure specifications for online transactions.

steps.what: Inspect funnel metrics, checkout settings and service issues for specification evidence.
Discuss customer journeys, operational constraints and competing requirements with stakeholders.
Set pricing, discount and checkout requirements within commercial authority.
Approve security and data-handling requirements with privacy input where needed.
Write the specification with traceable requirements, acceptance tests and unresolved questions.

loop.input: Recorded requirements, approved decisions and a controlled specification template
loop.output: A source-linked specification draft, acceptance tests and explicit unanswered questions
loop.check: Require a source for each requirement; check coverage, contradictions and testability without inventing decisions.
loop.stop: One draft and one revision; unresolved conflicts remain open for the named decision owner.
loop.why_not_simpler: Requirements arrive as prose with ambiguity and dependencies that fixed document assembly cannot reliably resolve.

steps.what: Resolve scope conflicts and approve a buildable specification.
Version the approved specification and create linked implementation work items.

tasks.design: A deterministic generator assembles permitted evidence from the {BI}, {ECOMMERCE} and {HELPDESK} into a controlled template in the {DOCS}. A bounded drafting loop links requirements to approved decisions, proposes acceptance tests and exposes gaps. Existing approval and versioning features publish the baseline and create linked work items in the {PROJECT}.
tasks.previous_blocker: Requirements were scattered across conversations, policy documents and system settings. Templates standardised headings but did little to expose contradictory or missing decisions.
tasks.enabler_now: Structured evidence assembly and bounded drafting can produce traceable specifications cheaply. Existing document approval and work-item features handle the handoff.
tasks.still_hard: Pricing tradeoffs, usability priorities and security exceptions require accountable decisions. GDPR and the EU AI Act apply as relevant; a drafting tool does not establish legal compliance.
tasks.human_edge: Find the real customer problem, negotiate competing constraints and reject requirements that are precise but commercially wrong.

ambition.what: Pre-build checkout readiness review for small campaign launches

tasks.altitude: Less time goes into formatting specifications and copying decisions into work items. The strategist can lead acceptance-criteria reviews and surface unresolved choices earlier; commercial, security and scope approvals stay with their existing owners.

reach.learn: Requirement traceability, interface contracts and verifiable acceptance criteria
Usability research, accessible interaction states and failure recovery
Discount precedence, order lifecycle and operational constraints

evidence.claim: Evidence assembly, document versioning and work-item creation can use deterministic generation and configured workflows.
A bounded drafting loop can prepare specifications while commercial and security decisions remain human; no direct case appears in the digest.
The digest documents a report containing non-existent sources, supporting explicit source verification in generated documents.

assumptions: Scope covers a reusable specification and approval workflow for one commerce journey.
Step shares, remaining time and build ranges are planning estimates.
Commercial, security and product approval roles already exist, even if one person fills several roles.
The judgement-heavy prior is credible; document preparation can still change substantially.
Drafting uses approved internal material without customer-level records.
The access range includes consultation if changed responsibilities or monitoring trigger national rules; a formal process may take longer.
unknowns: Which templates, approval routes and security standards are already mandatory?
Who has authority over pricing, security exceptions and scope?
Are current checkout settings and funnel metrics accessible?
Which privacy reviews and national consultation requirements apply?
Can approved requirements be linked to implementation work items without manual copying?
research_questions: Which missing or contradictory requirements cause the most implementation rework?
Can existing document templates and approval features cover the workflow?
Does the draft preserve every approved constraint without adding unsupported requirements?
Can developers and testers implement the specification without repeated clarification?
new_work: Verify requirement sources and proposed acceptance tests.
Resolve contradictory inputs with the responsible decision owners.
Maintain templates, policy references and approval routes.
Track changes between approved requirements and delivered behaviour.
Review model access and retention settings for internal documents.

role.altitude: The week shifts from assembling models, documents and system settings toward testing commercial assumptions, improving customer journeys and validating releases. The strategist can lead scenario and acceptance reviews; spending, service promises, security exceptions and deployment retain explicit approval owners.
reach: Marketing manager: prepare evidence for spending choices and campaign promises.
Market research analyst: design incrementality tests and interpret uncertainty.
Web and digital interface designer: validate accessible transaction and service journeys.
Technical writer: turn decisions into traceable, testable requirements.
Online merchant: connect checkout behaviour to order handling and commercial policy.
skills_to_grow: Data definitions, reconciliation and interface contracts
Accessible journey design and usability testing
Review of generated text and code against independent evidence
GDPR-aware data use and relevant EU AI Act obligations
role.ambitious_version: A search marketing strategist who links acquisition economics to checkout and service outcomes, proposes frequent evidence-based improvements and carries validated requirements through to accepted releases.
